name: Single-Leg Eccentric Hamstring Curl
trains: Hamstring eccentric strength for sprint athletes; braking and late-swing control
equipment: Leg curl machine; partner or trainer assist
cues: Partner helps lift the load up, athlete lowers it on one leg only; use a load too heavy to curl up alone; slow, controlled lowering

name: Single-Leg Eccentric Calf Raise
trains: Achilles and calf eccentric strength at full lengthening
cues: Rise up on two feet, lower on one; control the last inch or two as the heel drops fully below the step with the foot behind the body

name: Long-Duration Isometric Lunge
trains: Single-leg isometric strength and positional endurance
cues: Hold a split-stance lunge under load for a long duration; keep the front heel tall and hips and shoulders stacked and aligned

name: Trap Bar Isometric Hold
trains: Force production and bracing strength in a hinge position
cues: Set up in a strong trap bar position and hold; on-screen prescription was 3 sets of 10 seconds
programming: 3 sets x 10 sec (as shown on screen)

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
trains: Eccentric hamstring strength and injury resilience
cues: Partner pins the ankles; lower the body toward the floor as slowly as possible under hamstring control, then push back up; shown at 3 sets of 5 reps
programming: 3 sets x 5 reps (as shown on screen)

name: Step Box Jump
trains: Reactive strength and quick ground contact
cues: Step off and jump onto the box with minimal ground time; stay springy rather than sinking into the landing

name: Single-Leg Ball-Drop Plyometric on 45-Degree Hyperextension Bench
trains: Hamstring reactive strength in deep hip flexion, where sprint strains typically happen
cues: Anchored on one leg on the bench, drop the torso to catch a heavy medicine ball, then rebound back up immediately on the catch; keep the trunk braced

name: Cable-Resisted Eccentric Leg Extension in High Hip Flexion
trains: Hamstring strength at long lengths and high hip flexion angles
cues: Lying on the back with the hip flexed high, a trainer assists while the athlete resists the cable on the way out; train the hamstrings in flexion, not just in neutral

name: Straight Leg Bridge
trains: Posterior chain activation linking hamstrings and glutes before sprinting
cues: Used as a warm-up activation piece before high-speed work so the nervous system recruits hamstrings and glutes together

name: Wall Drill (Acceleration Wall Series)
trains: Acceleration posture and front-side mechanics
cues: Drive the knee only to about 90 degrees, toe up, punch the foot down under the hip and switch fast; if the knee travels higher the pelvis tips, the foot lands in front, and turnover slows

name: Hip Flexion Overcoming Isometric into Pad (3-Bucket Position)
trains: End-range hip flexion strength (iliopsoas) for front-side sprint mechanics
equipment: Bar and pad; resistance band on the foot
cues: Stack the joints vertically, heel of the stance leg lifted, swing knee driven just above hip height into the pad; push maximally into the pad; a band on the foot adds a resisted dorsiflexion pull
programming: 3-4 sets x 1 rep x 8-10 sec per leg

name: Butterfly PAILs/RAILs
trains: Groin and hip internal/external range under tension
cues: Seated against a wall in butterfly position; progressively load and then contract into the end range

name: ELDOA L5-S1
trains: Low back decompression and spinal positioning
cues: Lie on the floor with legs up the wall and arms extended in the prescribed ELDOA posture; breathe and push length through the crown of the head

name: Acupuncture Mat Standing
trains: Foot sensation and prep for the feet before training
cues: Stand barefoot on the mat as part of the pre-training warm-up sequence

name: Prone Shoulder Abduction with Internal Rotation
trains: Shoulder mobility and control
cues: Lie face down with the arms out; lift into abduction with internal rotation through a controlled range

name: Psoas Fascial Stretch
trains: Hip flexor (psoas) length and fascial release
cues: Kneeling lunge position with an arm reach; settle in and breathe while the front of the hip opens

name: Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat (Eccentric Overload)
trains: Single-leg eccentric strength, tendon stiffness and braking ability
cues: First rep: lower over a full 10 seconds holding both heavy dumbbells to your deepest range, then drop one dumbbell and finish the remaining reps fighting to stay stable and stacked, ribs over pelvis

name: Kneeling Medicine Ball Catch
trains: Reactive hamstring work that mirrors how the hamstrings absorb force late in the sprint swing
cues: From a tall kneeling ready position, catch the partner's throw and get the ball back out of the hands as fast as possible; keep the ribcage down

name: Kneeling Start Sprint
trains: Acceleration and explosive starts
cues: Set the hips where they can push from; on the coach's command, explode out of a kneeling start into a sprint

name: Clean (Teaching Progression)
trains: Full-body power through a hip-driven pull
cues: Teach the bar path first, then make the hips dynamic in the pull and finish into a high pull; keep it athletic rather than chasing perfect technique before adding load

name: Supine Feet-Elevated Banded Hip Flexion
trains: Hip flexor control plus hip extension strength for runners; single-leg pelvic control
cues: Lying on the back with feet up on a box and a band looped around the feet, pull the feet up and out against the band with knees bent; elevating the feet raises the posterior chain demand
programming: 2-3 sets x 8-10 reps per side (as stated by creator)

name: Banded Hip Flexor Stretch
trains: Hip flexor length with active control
cues: Band-assisted hip flexor stretch set up on a bench; treat tight hip flexors as a strength and control problem, not just a stretching problem

name: Banded Glute Bridge
trains: Glute strength as part of hip flexor health
cues: Bridge with a band around the legs; drive through the heels and finish with the glutes

name: Band-Resisted Acceleration March (Low Position)
trains: Acceleration posture: full-body power angle from head to toe
equipment: Resistance band; coach to hold band
cues: Lean the whole body into a low power angle on the balls of the feet rather than folding only at the waist, then march forward holding the position against band resistance

name: Band Lying Hamstring Curl
trains: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion without a curl machine
equipment: Resistance band anchored to a sled
cues: Lie down and curl the heel against band resistance anchored low behind you

name: Glute Bridge
trains: Hamstring and glute work through hip extension
cues: Bridge up driving through the heels; used alongside knee-flexion work so hamstrings are trained both ways

name: Band Seated Hamstring Curl
trains: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion without a curl machine
cues: Seated on a bench, curl the lower leg against the band's pull

name: Cable Knee Drive
trains: Hip flexor strength for faster thigh recovery, stride frequency and knee drive
cues: Cable attached low at the ankle; drive the knee up fast and under control; the creator's preferred pick of five hip flexor exercises in the post

name: Hip Flexor Crunch
trains: Hip flexor strength
cues: Crunch-style hip flexion movement from the creator's hip flexor series; on-screen rep scheme was shown in the video

name: Banded Hip Flexor In-and-Out
trains: Hip flexor strength through a range of motion
cues: Band-resisted in-and-out hip flexion movement from the creator's hip flexor series

name: ATG Split Squat
trains: Knee and hip strength through a deep split-squat range
cues: Deep split squat with the front knee travelling well over the toes, controlled down and up

name: Copenhagen Plank Hold
trains: Adductor and hip stability
cues: Side plank with the top leg supported on a bench; hold the position with a straight line from head to feet

name: Slider Hip Flexion
trains: Hip flexor strength and control
cues: Sliding hip flexion movement from the creator's hip flexor series

name: Yielding Isometric Hold
trains: Connective tissue and tendon capacity through long heavy holds
cues: Hold a heavy load in position for long durations, starting around 30 seconds and building toward a minute or more

name: Overcoming Isometric
trains: Muscle activation and joint prep before training
cues: Push or pull maximally against something that cannot move; short, full-effort contractions

name: Ballistic Pulse Isometric
trains: Fast-twitch activation and the ability to relax quickly
cues: Short ballistic pulses into an immovable resistance; switch on and off as fast as possible

name: Ballistic Catch Isometric
trains: Fast-twitch strength caught near end range
cues: Move fast and then catch and hold in a compromised, near end-range position

name: Oscillating Isometric
trains: Max fast-twitch recruitment, speed and coordination
cues: Rapid-fire repeated contractions with even faster relaxation between them
programming: 3-5 sec of as many reps as possible

name: Banded Explosive Lunge
trains: Unilateral leg power for a quick first step
cues: Explosive lunge with a band adding resistance; attack the ground and rebound

name: Single-Leg Clean
trains: Full-body power and posterior chain strength on one leg
cues: Clean the weight from the floor on a single-leg emphasis pattern; stay tall and balanced through the pull

name: Barbell Step-Up
trains: Single-leg strength and stability for legs and glutes
cues: Step up onto the box under a barbell, driving through the whole foot and standing fully tall

name: Banded Quick Step-Up
trains: Plyometric step-up speed and power
cues: Fast, springy step-ups against band resistance; minimal ground and box contact time

name: Hurdle Hops
trains: Explosive power, agility and coordination
cues: Repeated jumps over hurdles with quick, elastic contacts

name: Medicine Ball Slam
trains: Core power through the trunk
cues: Slam the ball down hard from overhead, bracing the whole trunk

name: Kneeling Hip Hinge
trains: Hip mobility through a hinge pattern
cues: Kneel on a block holding a kettlebell and hinge at the hips under control

name: Side-Lying Hip Stretch
trains: Hip mobility
cues: Lie on the side and work the hip through the stretch position shown in the tutorial

name: Down Dog to Lunge Reach
trains: Full-body mobility: hips, spine and shoulders
cues: Move from a downward dog into a low lunge and reach one arm up, rotating through the trunk

name: Barbell Split Squat
trains: Lower-body single-leg strength and stability
cues: Split squat under a barbell; torso tall, controlled depth, drive up through the front leg

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
trains: Back and arm strength
cues: Band under the knees or feet to assist the pull-up through a full range

name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
trains: Hip hinge mechanics, hamstring and glute strength, balance
cues: Hinge on one leg holding a dumbbell; hips back, back flat, control the whole way down and up

name: Box Jump
trains: Explosive lower-body power
cues: Jump onto stacked boxes, land quietly and stand tall

name: Agility Ladder Footwork
trains: Foot speed and coordination
cues: Fast, precise patterns through the ladder; stay light on the feet

name: Flying 10-Yard Sprint
trains: Max velocity sprinting
cues: Build in, then sprint the flying 10-yard zone at full speed; the featured athlete's 0.89s was down from 1.02 two years earlier

name: Vertical Jump + Single-Leg Broad Jump
trains: Linked plyometric power
cues: Vertical jump straight into a single-leg broad jump; carry the height into distance

name: Broad Jump + Pogo Hop
trains: Elastic power pairing
cues: Broad jump followed immediately by pogo hops; stay springy between the two

name: Consecutive Single-Leg Broad Jump with Bounce
trains: Single-leg elastic power
cues: Repeated single-leg broad jumps with a bounce between each; same leg rhythm and posture throughout

name: Split Stance Pogo Hops
trains: Ankle stiffness and split-stance elasticity
cues: Pogo hops from a split stance; quick, low-amplitude contacts

name: Suitcase March on Foam
trains: Trunk stability with the spine long and stable
equipment: Foam pad; weight in one hand
cues: March in place on foam holding a weight at one side; do not let the trunk lean or rotate

name: Anti-Rotation Back Pedal
trains: Trunk anti-rotation stability
cues: Back pedal while resisting rotation from the band or cable pull

name: Plank Press-Up
trains: Trunk and shoulder stability
cues: From a plank, press between forearm and high plank positions without the hips shifting

name: Plank Bird Dog
trains: Trunk stability with opposite arm and leg reach
cues: In a plank or quadruped position, extend opposite arm and leg without the pelvis rotating

name: Hyperextension with Reach
trains: Posterior chain and trunk work with a reach
cues: Hyperextend and reach; keep the spine long rather than cranking through the low back

name: Plank Walkout
trains: Trunk stability through a long lever
cues: Walk the hands out from a plank as far as control allows and walk back in

name: Stir the Pot
trains: Trunk stability on an unstable surface
cues: Forearms on a stability ball in a plank; circle the ball in both directions without the trunk moving

name: Standing Hip Flexor Stretch with Rotation
trains: Hip flexor length and control
equipment: Smith machine or support for balance
cues: Standing, pull the heel toward the glute and rotate the torso; finish with a short hold at the top

name: Kneeling Hip Stretch
trains: Hip mobility
cues: Kneeling hip stretch as the opener of the track-side hip routine

name: Hip Rockers
trains: Hip mobility through rocking ranges
cues: Rock the hips through the ranges shown on screen in the creator's hip routine

name: Single-Leg Raise
trains: Hip flexor and core control
cues: Raise one leg under control as shown in the routine; on-screen reps were given in the video

name: External Hip Hold
trains: Hip external rotation strength and control
cues: Hold the externally rotated hip position shown in the routine

name: Single-Leg Bridge
trains: Glute and hamstring strength on one leg
cues: Bridge up on one leg, pelvis level throughout

name: Kneeling Switches
trains: Hip mobility and internal/external rotation transitions
cues: From kneeling, switch the hips side to side under control

name: Lateral Box Jump
trains: Lateral power, agility and jump height
cues: Jump laterally between boxes; land balanced and rebound

name: Hurdle Slalom Hops
trains: Lateral agility and elastic hops
cues: Hop side to side through a hurdle slalom pattern

name: Skater Tuck Jump
trains: Lateral power with a tuck finish
cues: Skater jumps combined with tuck jumps in a four-cone complex

name: Rapid Plate Hops
trains: Ankle stiffness and rapid contacts
cues: Quick hops on and off plates with minimal ground time

name: Hurdle Skater Hop
trains: Lateral power over a hurdle
cues: Skater-style lateral jumps clearing a hurdle

name: Block Start
trains: Acceleration out of the blocks
cues: Push violently off the lead pedal, project the hips horizontally, drive the knee forward; fewer words from the coach, more focus from the athlete

name: Elevated Pigeon Stretch
trains: Hip external rotation and low back mobility
cues: Shin up on an elevated surface for a deeper pigeon stretch; can also be done on the floor

name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
trains: Hip internal and external rotation mobility
cues: Sit in the 90/90 position and work both hips as the opener of a hip prep warm-up

name: Kettlebell Hip Shift
trains: Hip mobility and weight shifting in deep positions
cues: Use the kettlebell as a counterbalance to shift the hips through deep ranges

name: World's Greatest Stretch (Modified)
trains: Full-body mobility: hips, thoracic spine, hamstrings
cues: Modified version of the classic sequence: lunge, elbow drop, rotation and reach

name: Quadruped Hip CARs
trains: Controlled articular rotations for hip joint health
cues: On all fours, circle the hip through its full controlled range without the pelvis moving

name: Platform Drop Reactive Landing
trains: Reactive force absorption and fast ground reaction for speed and change of direction
cues: Drop off the platform and react to the ground as fast as possible on landing; the quicker the reaction, the more force you can put back into the ground when sprinting

name: Explosive Step-Up
trains: Hip and knee stability plus violent force into a platform
cues: Step up onto the platform striking it violently; pull yourself up with the hip and knee stabilising, core tight

name: Stability Ball Mountain Climber
trains: Core stability and body control under time under tension
cues: Plank with hands on a stability ball and feet elevated on a box; drive the knees toward the chest in a rapid alternating climber without losing position
